main_text.p: dictionem edifcere pertentabant, nisi perrari admodum ac fortuito vir viro congredientes. Nam Cares per totam Græciam erraverunt stipendia merentes. Quare barbari ex illo sunt appellati, ex quo ex Græcia milites erant. At postea quam apud insulas habitarunt, id multum in eis eminuit. Inde in Asiam profecti, nec ibi sine Græcis vivere potuerunt. Nam Jones cum eis ac Dores trajicere. Ab eadem quoque causa barbarismus dictus est. Tum enim in his dicere consuevimus, qui male græcissant: non autem in iis, qui Caricè loquuntur. Sic etiam barbariloquos & barbari sermonis homines, eos accipere debemus, qui male Græca pronunciant. Carico autem more barbarismū ad Græcæ orationis artem transtulerunt, & solœcismum: sive id nomen à Solis ductum sit, sive alio modo: Hæc omnia Strabo. Græca verba circa finem sic sonant: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς χαρίζειν, καὶ τὸ (forte τῆς) βαρβαρίζειν, μετήνεγκαν εἰς τὰς περὶ Ἑλληνισμὸν τέχνας καὶ τὸ σολοικίζειν, εἶτ' ἀπὸ Σόλων, εἴτ' ἄλλως τὸ ὄνομα τῷ τότε πεπλασμένον.
¶ Carni, Carniolani, & Carinthii usque ad Dravum, Illyricè loquuntur.

page.notes: Greek text is copied from a small, faint scan; accents and breathings in the first line and the words after "forte" are uncertain. The printed "Qnare" has a Q ligature and is read as "Quare". Line-end hyphens in "perra-ri", "po-tuerunt", "traje-cere", "di-ctus", "consuevi-mus", "barbariloquos", "acci-pere", "pronunci-ant" and "Græ-cæ" are joined. Partly obscured top-left letters of the first word are read as "dictionem" with [?] not required; the lead letter may be damaged. Text at the top begins mid-sentence, so the first paragraph is a continuation.
